why_this_matters: Day 123 sits in Phase 7 (Statistics), whose goal is: Describe data, quantify uncertainty and test hypotheses correctly. Today's core material - Statistic as a random variable, Distribution of the sample mean, Standard error and the sqrt(n) law - is the vocabulary the rest of the phase is built on. Learners who skip the concept and jump to copying code usually stall two weeks later; the goal here is that you can explain what you did, not just that it ran.

code.heading: shapiro wilk Test on Normal Distribution Gaussian Distribution
code.code:
# shapiro Wilk Test
statistic, p = stats.shapiro(df['age'])

# print the results using if else
if p > 0.05:
    print(f'p-value: {p}, Sample looks Gaussian/Normally Distributed (fail to reject H0)')
else:
    print(f'p-value: {p}, Sample does not look Gaussian/Normally Distributed (reject H0)')

code.heading: shapiro wilk Test on Normal Distribution Gaussian Distribution
1. One-sample T-test
code.code:
import scipy.stats as stats

# sample data
x = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

# known population mean
mu = 4

# perform one sample t-test
t_statistic, p = stats.ttest_1samp(x, mu)

# print results
print('t-statistic:', t_statistic)
print('p-value:', p)

# print the results using if else
if p > 0.05:
    print(f'p-value: {p}, Sample mean is equal to population mean (fail to reject H0)')
else:
    print(f'p-value: {p}, Sample mean is not equal to population mean (reject H0)')

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using Statistic as a random variable on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).
